1223	func (s *vizServer) handleGraph(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1224		// `limit` is the number of symbols to RENDER (the node-count slider drives it).
1225		// We load a wider pool, rank it by degree, and keep the top `limit` so the view
1226		// is always the most-connected slice at any size the user picks. vizQueryLimit
1227		// owns the shared policy: 0 ("render all") and oversized values clamp to the
1228		// vizGraphMaxView safety ceiling.
1229		view := vizQueryLimit(r, vizGraphViewCap)
1230		// Scale the edge budget with the node count so a bigger view isn't artificially
1231		// sparse. ~4 edges/node reads as a real constellation; floored so small views
1232		// still show structure, ceilinged so a huge view can't blow up payload/draw.
1233		edgeCap := view * 4
1234		if edgeCap < 12000 {
1235			edgeCap = 12000
1236		}
1237		if edgeCap > vizGraphMaxEdges {
1238			edgeCap = vizGraphMaxEdges
1239		}
1240		resp := vizGraphResp{Nodes: []vizNode{}, Edges: []vizEdge{}}
1241		sem := s.semanticSource()
1242		if sem == nil {
1243			resp.Warnings = append(resp.Warnings, "no code graph yet — run `"+base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, base.SemanticIndexVerb)+"`")
1244			writeJSONHTTP(w, http.StatusOK, resp)
1245			return
1246		}
1247		pool := view * 3
1248		if pool < 4000 {
1249			pool = 4000
1250		}
1251		// The pool is ranking headroom, not render size — cap it at the same
1252		// safety ceiling so a maxed slider can't triple the documented worst case.
1253		// As view approaches the ceiling the headroom shrinks until view == pool,
1254		// where ranking degenerates to keep-everything — which is exactly what
1255		// "render all" means at that size.
1256		if pool > vizGraphMaxView {
1257			pool = vizGraphMaxView
1258		}
1259		syms, err := s.semanticSymbolPool(sem, pool)
1260		if err != nil {
1261			resp.Warnings = append(resp.Warnings, "code graph symbols: "+err.Error())
1262			writeJSONHTTP(w, http.StatusOK, resp)
1263			return
1264		}
1265		if len(syms) == 0 {
1266			resp.Warnings = append(resp.Warnings, "the code index has no symbols yet — run `"+base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, base.SemanticIndexVerb)+"`")
1267			writeJSONHTTP(w, http.StatusOK, resp)
1268			return
1269		}
1270		resp.Total = sem.Symbols
1271	
1272		// Rank the pool by degree so any `view` size keeps the most-connected symbols
1273		// (semstore.LoadSymbols returns storage order, so an unranked cap keeps leaves).
1274		poolSet := make(map[string]bool, len(syms))
1275		for i := range syms {
1276			poolSet[syms[i].ID] = true
1277		}
1278		// Relations feed degree ranking (which wants a wider sample than the render
1279		// budget) and then edge selection (hard-capped at edgeCap). Past a few
1280		// multiples of the max edge budget, extra relations barely move the ranking
1281		// but cost real load/merge time — ceiling the fetch keeps a 300k-node
1282		// request from pulling millions of rows it can never render.
1283		relLimit := pool * 4
1284		if relLimit > 4*vizGraphMaxEdges {
1285			relLimit = 4 * vizGraphMaxEdges
1286		}
1287		var rels []semanticRecord
1288		if r, rerr := s.relationsForSymbols(sem, syms, relLimit); rerr != nil {
1289			resp.Warnings = append(resp.Warnings, "relations: "+rerr.Error())
1290		} else {
1291			rels = r
1292		}
1293		deg := make(map[string]int, len(syms))
1294		for i := range rels {
1295			e := rels[i]
1296			if poolSet[e.FromID] && poolSet[e.ToID] {
1297				deg[e.FromID]++
1298				deg[e.ToID]++
1299			}
1300		}
1301		kept := syms
1302		if view > 0 && len(syms) > view {
1303			ranked := make([]semanticRecord, len(syms))
1304			copy(ranked, syms)
1305			sort.SliceStable(ranked, func(i, j int) bool { return deg[ranked[i].ID] > deg[ranked[j].ID] })
1306			kept = ranked[:view]
1307		}
1308		keptSet := make(map[string]bool, len(kept))
1309		for i := range kept {
1310			resp.Nodes = append(resp.Nodes, nodeJSON(kept[i]))
1311			keptSet[kept[i].ID] = true
1312		}
1313		// Cap edges for render/sim budget, but choose them for COVERAGE first: a naive
1314		// first-N cap piles all edges onto a few hubs and leaves most nodes edgeless, so
1315		// they fly apart under repulsion and the whole graph fits to a dot. Pass 1 keeps
1316		// edges that connect a still-unconnected node; pass 2 fills the remaining budget.
1317		seen := make(map[string]bool)
1318		covered := make(map[string]int)
1319		addEdge := func(e semanticRecord) {
1320			k := vizEdgeKey(e.FromID, e.ToID)
1321			if seen[k] {
1322				return
1323			}
1324			seen[k] = true
1325			resp.Edges = append(resp.Edges, edgeJSON(e))
1326			covered[e.FromID]++
1327			covered[e.ToID]++
1328		}
1329		for i := range rels {
1330			if len(resp.Edges) >= edgeCap {
1331				break
1332			}
1333			e := rels[i]
1334			if keptSet[e.FromID] && keptSet[e.ToID] && (covered[e.FromID] == 0 || covered[e.ToID] == 0) {
1335				addEdge(e)
1336			}
1337		}
1338		for i := range rels {
1339			if len(resp.Edges) >= edgeCap {
1340				break
1341			}
1342			e := rels[i]
1343			if keptSet[e.FromID] && keptSet[e.ToID] {
1344				addEdge(e)
1345			}
1346		}
1347		resp.Truncated = sem.Symbols > len(kept)
1348		writeJSONHTTP(w, http.StatusOK, resp)

1351	func (s *vizServer) handleNode(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1352		id := strings.TrimSpace(r.URL.Query().Get("id"))
1353		resp := vizNodeResp{Neighbors: []vizNode{}, Relations: []vizEdge{}}
1354		if id == "" {
1355			writeJSONHTTP(w, http.StatusBadRequest, vizNodeResp{Warnings: []string{"missing id"}})
1356			return
1357		}
1358		sem := s.semanticSource()
1359		if sem == nil {
1360			resp.Warnings = append(resp.Warnings, "no code graph")
1361			writeJSONHTTP(w, http.StatusOK, resp)
1362			return
1363		}
1364		node, neighbors, rels, err := s.nodeDetail(sem, id)
1365		if err != nil {
1366			resp.Warnings = append(resp.Warnings, err.Error())
1367			writeJSONHTTP(w, http.StatusOK, resp)
1368			return
1369		}
1370		if node == nil {
1371			writeJSONHTTP(w, http.StatusNotFound, vizNodeResp{Neighbors: []vizNode{}, Relations: []vizEdge{}, Warnings: []string{"symbol not found: " + id}})
1372			return
1373		}
1374		resp.Symbol = nodeJSON(*node)
1375		resp.Snippet = node.Blob
1376		if l := s.sourceLink(node.FilePath, node.StartLine); l != "" {
1377			resp.Link = l
1378			resp.LinkLabel = "View source"
1379		}
1380		for i := range neighbors {
1381			resp.Neighbors = append(resp.Neighbors, nodeJSON(neighbors[i]))
1382		}
1383		for i := range rels {
1384			resp.Relations = append(resp.Relations, edgeJSON(rels[i]))
1385		}
1386		writeJSONHTTP(w, http.StatusOK, resp)
1387	}

1389	func (s *vizServer) handleSearch(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1390		q := strings.TrimSpace(r.URL.Query().Get("q"))
1391		limit := 25
1392		if v := r.URL.Query().Get("limit"); v != "" {
1393			if n, err := strconv.Atoi(v); err == nil && n > 0 {
1394				limit = n
1395			}
1396		}
1397		// Hits render in the rail / ⌘K palette, so anything beyond a few hundred
1398		// per source is never useful — cap it so a crafted ?limit can't force an
1399		// arbitrarily expensive retrieval.
1400		if limit > vizSearchMaxHits {
1401			limit = vizSearchMaxHits
1402		}
1403		resp := vizSearchResp{Hits: []vizHit{}}
1404		if q == "" {
1405			writeJSONHTTP(w, http.StatusOK, resp)
1406			return
1407		}
1408		// Symbol matches first so ⌘K / rail search can jump straight to a graph node.
1409		if sem := s.semanticSource(); sem != nil {
1410			if syms, _, _, err := semstore.ContextFacts(s.brainDir, sem, q, limit, 0); err == nil {
1411				for _, sy := range syms {
1412					resp.Hits = append(resp.Hits, vizHit{Source: "symbol", ID: sy.ID, Title: sy.Name, Text: sy.QualifiedName, Kind: sy.Kind, Path: sy.FilePath, Line: sy.StartLine})
1413				}
1414			}
1415		}
1416		// Memory hits (facts / history / docs), same code path as `entire brain search`.
1417		if u, err := retrieveUnified(s.repoDir, s.brainDir, s.branch, q, limit, retrieval.ModeLexical); err == nil {
1418			for _, h := range u {
1419				text := h.Text
1420				if h.VerificationRequired {
1421					text = "VERIFY AGAINST CURRENT EVIDENCE: " + text
1422				}
1423				resp.Hits = append(resp.Hits, vizHit{Source: h.Source, ID: h.ID, Title: h.Heading, Text: text, Path: h.Path, Line: h.Line, Score: h.Score})
1424			}
1425		}
1426		writeJSONHTTP(w, http.StatusOK, resp)
1427	}

1429	// relationsForSymbols returns relations INCIDENT to the given symbols — either
1430	// endpoint may be outside the set (the queries match from_id OR to_id); callers
1431	// that need both endpoints inside filter the result themselves. Mirrors the
1432	// SQLite-vs-snapshot branch semstore.ContextFacts uses (semantic.go).
1433	func (s *vizServer) relationsForSymbols(sem *semanticSourceManifest, syms []semanticRecord, limit int) ([]semanticRecord, error) {
1434		storePath, err := semstore.ValidateDeclaredStore(s.brainDir, sem)
1435		if err != nil {
1436			return nil, err
1437		}
1438		return semstore.FindRelationsForSymbolsInSQLite(storePath, syms, limit)
1439	}
1440	
1441	// nodeDetail resolves one symbol by exact id plus its relations and neighbors,
1442	// mirroring semstore.ContextFacts but seeded by id rather than a search query.
1443	func (s *vizServer) nodeDetail(sem *semanticSourceManifest, id string) (*semanticRecord, []semanticRecord, []semanticRecord, error) {
1444		const limit = 80
1445		storePath, err := semstore.ValidateDeclaredStore(s.brainDir, sem)
1446		if err != nil {
1447			return nil, nil, nil, err
1448		}
1449		byID, err := semstore.LoadSymbolsByIDsSQLite(storePath, []string{id})
1450		if err != nil {
1451			return nil, nil, nil, err
1452		}
1453		node, ok := byID[id]
1454		if !ok {
1455			return nil, nil, nil, nil
1456		}
1457		rels, err := semstore.FindRelationsForSymbolsInSQLite(storePath, []semanticRecord{node}, limit*4)
1458		if err != nil {
1459			return nil, nil, nil, err
1460		}
1461		neighbors, err := s.resolveNeighbors(node, rels, func(ids []string) (map[string]semanticRecord, error) {
1462			return semstore.LoadSymbolsByIDsSQLite(storePath, ids)
1463		}, limit)
1464		if err != nil {
1465			return nil, nil, nil, err
1466		}
1467		return &node, neighbors, rels, nil
1468	}
1469	
1470	func (s *vizServer) resolveNeighbors(node semanticRecord, rels []semanticRecord, load func([]string) (map[string]semanticRecord, error), limit int) ([]semanticRecord, error) {
1471		ids := semstore.NeighborCandidateIDs([]semanticRecord{node}, rels)
1472		if len(ids) == 0 {
1473			return nil, nil
1474		}
1475		byID, err := load(ids)
1476		if err != nil {
1477			return nil, err
1478		}
1479		return semstore.ResolveContextNeighbors([]semanticRecord{node}, rels, byID, limit), nil
1480	}

1482	func writeJSONHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, code int, v any) {
1483		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
1484		w.WriteHeader(code)
1485		_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v)
1486	}

1488	// openBrowser best-effort opens url in the default browser. Failure never fails
1489	// the command — the URL is already printed for manual navigation.
1490	func openBrowser(url string) {
1491		var c *exec.Cmd
1492		switch runtime.GOOS {
1493		case "darwin":
1494			c = exec.Command("open", url)
1495		case "windows":
1496			c = exec.Command("rundll32", "url.dll,FileProtocolHandler", url)
1497		default:
1498			c = exec.Command("xdg-open", url)
1499		}
1500		_ = c.Start()
1501	}

package cli

import bmanifest "github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/cli/internal/manifest"

// The brain-manifest schema lives in internal/cli/internal/manifest
// (COR-2268). These aliases keep the package-local spellings compiling
// while command clusters move out; they retire with the cli package.
type (
	exportManifest           = bmanifest.Manifest
	exportBranch             = bmanifest.Branch
	exportSession            = bmanifest.Session
	exportAuthor             = bmanifest.Author
	brainSources             = bmanifest.Sources
	sessionSourceManifest    = bmanifest.SessionSource

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

Weighing this against the orchestrator's budget guidance of roughly 8-11 injected functions, I'm realizing the inject-based alternative would force Deps wiring into nearly every visualization test, moved or staying, which clearly violates the no-rewrite constraint. After that I need to pin command/viz/main_test.go with clitest first, then carefully split the test files — moving viz_test.go into the new package while keeping three tests in a cli-side file.

    # type renames
    (r'\bvizServer\b', 'Server'),
    (r'\bvizNode\b', 'Node'),
    (r'\bvizEdge\b', 'Edge'),
    (r'\bvizGraphResp\b', 'GraphResp'),
    (r'\bvizNodeResp\b', 'NodeResp'),
    (r'\bvizCounts\b', 'Counts'),

    (r'\bvizSearchResp\b', 'SearchResp'),
    (r'\bvizGNode\b', 'GNode'),
    (r'\bvizGEdge\b', 'GEdge'),
    (r'\bvizFeatureGraph\b', 'FeatureGraph'),
    (r'\bvizReplayStep\b', 'ReplayStep'),
    (r'\bvizReplayResp\b', 'ReplayResp'),
    (r'\bcolorSession\b', 'ColorSession'),
    (r'\bcolorHistory\b', 'ColorHistory'),
    # methods
    (r'\bmux\(\)', 'Mux()'),
    (r'\) mux\(', ') Mux('),
    (r'\bhandleSummary\b', 'HandleSummary'),
    (r'\bhandleGraph\b', 'HandleGraph'),
    (r'\bhandleNode\b', 'HandleNode'),
    (r'\bhandleSearch\b', 'HandleSearch'),
    (r'\bhandleFacts\b', 'HandleFacts'),
    (r'\bhandleSessions\b', 'HandleSessions'),
    (r'\bhandleSessionReplay\b', 'HandleSessionReplay'),
    (r'\bhandleHistory\b', 'HandleHistory'),
    (r'\bhandleDocs\b', 'HandleDocs'),
    # alias -> importable types
    (r'\bexportManifest\b', 'bmanifest.Manifest'),
    (r'\bexportSession\b', 'bmanifest.Session'),
    (r'\bsemanticSourceManifest\b', 'bmanifest.SemanticSource'),
    (r'\bsemanticRecord\b', 'semstore.Record'),
    (r'\bfactRecord\b', 'factmerge.Record'),
    (r'\bhistoryRecord\b', 'historystore.Record'),
    (r'\bdocRecord\b', 'docstore.Record'),
    (r'\bsessionReadGuard\b', 'brainstore.SessionReadGuard'),
    (r'\bretrievalPrivacyPolicy\b', 'brainstore.RetrievalPrivacyPolicy'),
    # struct-literal keys in runViz
    (r'\brepoDir: repoDir, brainDir: brainDir, branch: branch, manifest: manifest,',
     'RepoDir: repoDir, BrainDir: brainDir, Branch: branch, Manifest: manifest, Deps: cfg.Deps,'),
    (r'\bguard: guard, guardObserved: !guard\.Empty\(\),', 'Guard: guard, GuardObserved: !guard.Empty(),'),
]
for pat, rep in subs:
    src = re.sub(pat, rep, src)
src = src.replace('package cli\n', 'package viz\n', 1)
open(path, 'w').write(src)
print('transformed')

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

def test_events(text):
    events = []
    for line in text.splitlines():
        try:
            events.append(json.loads(line))
        except ValueError:
            continue
    return events


def detected(result, case):

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--cases", default=str(Path(__file__).with_name("mutations.json")))
    parser.add_argument("--tags", default="")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    cases = json.loads(Path(args.cases).read_text())
    flags = ["-tags", args.tags] if args.tags else []
    for case in cases:
        source = (ROOT / case["file"]).resolve()
        source.relative_to(ROOT)
        original = source.read_text()
        if original.count(case["original"]) != 1:
            raise RuntimeError(f"mutation anchor is stale or ambiguous: {case['name']}")
        command = ["go", "test", *flags, "-json", "-count=1", "-timeout=2m",
                   "./internal/cli", "-run", "^" + re.escape(case["test"]) + "$"]
        baseline = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=180)
        if baseline.returncode or not any(e.get("Action") == "pass" and e.get("Test") == case["test"] for e in test_events(baseline.stdout)):
            raise RuntimeError(f"baseline did not pass: {case['name']}\n{baseline.stdout}\n{baseline.stderr}")
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="brain-mutation-") as temporary:
            directory = Path(temporary)
            replacement = directory / source.name
            replacement.write_text(original.replace(case["original"], case["replacement"], 1))
            overlay = directory / "overlay.json"
            overlay.write_text(json.dumps({"Replace": {str(source): str(replacement)}}))
            mutant_command = command[:2] + [f"-overlay={overlay}"] + command[2:]
            mutant = subprocess.run(mutant_command, cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=180)
            if not detected(mutant, case):
                raise RuntimeError(f"mutation was not caught by the intended assertion: {case['name']}\n{mutant.stdout}\n{mutant.stderr}")
        print(f"PASS: {case['name']} — clean baseline passes; intended regression fails", flush=True)

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

tools.name: Monitor
tools.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

Committed; working tree clean; not pushed. Final report in the recipe's format.

---

## COR-2268 viz cluster — report

**Branch / commit:** `cor-2268-cmd-viz2` (from `origin/main` @ 637c039a, post-#538) — commit `b0d0b2e3`.

**Preflights (recorded):** Brain dev build, BM25-only, durable_facts/task_briefs/recall supported — available. Graph entire-graph v0.6.0, full Go semantic coverage — available. Brief run; both required recalls retrieved (fact:b80d6f198d42a3c09bfdfc13 original closure map; fact:7d9e9ef8ac90463c144b029e engine surface).

**Moved files (prod):** `internal/cli/viz.go` → `internal/cli/command/viz/viz.go` (git rename, 73% similarity). New: `command/viz/deps.go` (Config/Deps), `command/viz/main_test.go` (clitest pin, created before any test move), cli-side `viz_config.go` (root wiring + `vizDeps()` + `commitVizRetrievalResponse`). `root.go` mounts `viz.New(vizConfig(opts))`.

**Deps seam — 5 injected funcs (budget ≤8):** AgentSurfaceTarget, ResolveFactsTarget (facts-package precedent names), BrainManifest (narrowed `buildBrainStatusReport` wrapper — brainreview BrainStatus precedent; the cli-private `brainStatusReport` type does not cross), RetrieveUnified, CommitRetrievalResponse (transport middleware piece; cli wrapper binds `beforeRetrievalResponsePrivacyEmissionCheck/Write` + `withLockedRetrievalPrivacyPolicies` — hook vars stayed single-homed in cli `retrieval_transport.go`, no swap sites renamed). No cli-private types cross. The probe's predicted `loadFreshHistory`/conversation-view seams never materialized — they live inside the one RetrieveUnified seam.

**Helpers sunk (symbol → new home), impact/grep evidence cited per symbol (Graph impact run on all; several hit cross-package name disambiguation, exact-spelling grep lists recorded as the supplementary evidence):**
- `excludedTranscriptPaths`, `loadSessionReadGuard`, `guardBlocksExportSession`, `guardExportSessions` → `bmanifest.ExcludedTranscriptPaths/LoadSessionReadGuard/GuardBlocksSession/GuardSessions` (manifest-typed; bmanifest already imports brainstore)
- `guardBlocksRecord` → `historystore.GuardBlocksRecord`
- `guardFactRecords`, `guardBlocksFact`, `guardBlocksFactAnchor` → `factstore.GuardRecords/GuardBlocksFact/GuardBlocksFactAnchor` (factmerge is top-level, cannot host)
- `firstNonEmpty` → `base.FirstNonEmpty`; `knownRepoDomainSlugs` → `base.KnownRepoDomainSlugs`; `commandErrorCode(+pattern)` → `cmdutil.CommandErrorCode`
- All cli call sites renamed (≈35 files incl. `retrieval.Deps`/`publish.Deps` wiring); no shims. Justified as the brainstore read-guard layer the recipe names as storage-domain; without the sink, every guard-exercising viz test would have needed fake-Deps rewrites.

**Tests:** inventory 3136 before → 3120 (cli) + 16 (viz), union exactly equal. 16 roots moved (15 from viz_test.go, 1 from viz_graph_regression_test.go) — all bodies IDENTICAL under the rename map. 11 viz-exercising roots stayed in cli (semantic-index / transport / tombstone fixtures): 5 IDENTICAL under the map; 6 DIFFER minimally and deliberately — `Deps: vizDeps()` added to 5 Server literals (TestVizFeatureHandlers_UnbuiltBrain, TestVizSecurityHeaders_AppliedToMux, TestVizNodePublicResponseUsesGraphStore, both TestVizAPIResponse\* transport roots) and TestCorruptTombstonesRefuseHandoffDashAndVizStartup re-pointed `runViz(...opts...)` → `viz.Run(..., vizConfig(opts), viz.Flags{NoOpen: true}, ...)` (brainreview.RunBrainReview precedent in the same transport file). Server/handlers/Run/Flags/SecurityHeaders exported for these callers.

**Scan guards (widened minimally, flagged):** `runnable_remedies_test.go` walk gained `command/viz`; its allowlist entry re-pointed to `command/viz/viz.go`. `tools/coverage/mutations.json` anchor re-pointed to the renamed `bmanifest.GuardSessions` line (tools/ci-bench untouched; pinned `TestMain` untouched). `versioned_state_test` walk NOT widened — viz has no persisted-state decoders (no `DisallowUnknownFields`).

**Gates (all run, real results):**
- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/cli/command/viz` — ok, 2.4s
- focused `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/cli -run 'TestViz|TestParseRepoFromKey|TestFindSemanticRelations|TestCorruptTombstones'` — ok, 2.6s
- `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` — exit 0
- ci-bench windows-production unittest — 41 tests, OK
- `mutation_check.py` — 4/4 PASS (after the anchor re-point; it correctly failed stale before)
- Full `go test -race -p=1 ./... -count=1 -timeout=30m` — ALL ok, exit 0 (internal/cli 436s); no split-run needed
- `gofmt -l -s` clean, `go vet ./...` clean (no oxfmt binary exists; CI gates on gofmt+vet per recorded memory)
